question: Should OpenClaw run targeted SQLite integrity checks for all canonical-index tables on every cold open, accepting additional startup work and a fail-closed outcome for unrecoverable table corruption?
rationale: The physical corruption described by the PR cannot be detected by schema text alone, but the chosen detection point is a permanent startup behavior change for durable user state and needs owner confirmation of the latency and availability tradeoff.

options.title: Measure then land
options.body: Capture cold-open timings on representative existing agent and shared-state databases and land this direct integrity strategy if the startup budget is acceptable.

options.title: Accept the conservative startup cost
options.body: Land now and explicitly accept slower cold opens in exchange for detecting canonical-looking but physically invalid indexes before writable use.

options.title: Pause for a narrower trigger
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers require a bounded detection strategy that avoids unconditional integrity scans without reintroducing hidden physical-index drift.

recommendation.title: Measure then land
recommendation.body: Capture cold-open timings on representative existing agent and shared-state databases and land this direct integrity strategy if the startup budget is acceptable.
